rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without excessive truncation risk. All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only gain is reducing t_last below 10 min. Keep the same wide window and temperature but shorten the gradient one step to test how much time can be saved before any critical pair, especially 6–7, drops toward 1.5.

The current method is very close to the 10 min target and the critical pair 6–7 is still just above full-credit threshold, so one more decrease in tG is the fastest way to probe the limit. This tests whether we can eliminate the remaining time penalty without losing resolution on the most compression-sensitive pair.

Lowering temperature made selectivity worse by collapsing peaks 5–6, so test the opposite direction to see whether a modest increase in T improves the crowded central cluster while preserving the sub-10 min runtime. This directly probes whether temperature can rescue the critical region better than slope alone.

Temperature changes hurt the crowded middle region, so keep T at 40 C and instead narrow the gradient window slightly from the strong high-organic end. This should make the gradient a bit shallower across the actual elution region, potentially improving the 6–7 separation while keeping all peaks within 10 min.

Narrowing the window improved the critical 6–7 pair while keeping t_last under 10 min, so continue one more step in the same direction. This should further shallow the gradient in the active elution zone and may push the last unresolved pair to full credit without incurring a time penalty.

The 6–7 pair responds strongly to slope/window, and lowering T at phi1 0.95 created a different selectivity pattern, so combine the improved 0.90 window with a 5 C lower temperature to see if 6–7 can be pushed to full credit while keeping t_last near 10 min. This probes a potentially better selectivity regime than any tried so far around the current best method.

Since lowering temperature near the best window collapses peaks 5–6, test the opposite direction at the same faster gradient to see whether higher T improves selectivity in the crowded central cluster. Temperature variation around the best region is clearly unfavorable, so return to 40 C and lengthen tG one step at phi1 0.90 to see if the critical 6–7 pair can reach full resolution while staying close to the 10 min target. This explores the likely optimum between the fully resolved but slightly slow phi1 0.85/14 and the faster but under-resolved phi1 0.90/14.

Injection 12 suggests raising phi0 is beneficial, and narrowing the upper end previously improved the critical 6–7 pair. Combining both changes should slightly shallow the gradient across the true elution window and may push 6–7 to full-credit resolution while keeping the last peak under 10 min.

With two injections left and several max-CRF methods already found, the best remaining use is to bracket the upper-window side around the strong phi0 0.15 condition. Testing phi1 0.90 at the same tG checks whether a slightly wider high-end window can preserve full resolution while offering a different robust optimum near the current best region.

For the final shot, probe just one more narrower window from the perfect 0.20/0.80/14 method to see whether the critical pair gains enough from the shallower gradient to offset any retention shift and still keep t_last under 10 min.
